scope: Read-only source and official contract review; no Gradle, CMake, native compilation, converter execution, ADB, VM, push, or GitHub writes by this reviewer. This is not runtime or publication acceptance.

official_contract.strategy: Run the pinned source official Dictionaries target with OPENCC_DICT_FORMAT=text using its built host converter. Preserve original ocd2 JSON files; do not package ConvertedConfigs text-mode JSON.

accepted_properties: Host wrapper builds only pinned OpenCC, statically, with Jieba/Python/tests/benchmark/docs/install disabled; it does not change Android JNI source or ABI configuration.
ExecOperations receives argument lists and asserts normal exit; no arbitrary installed opencc or handwritten conversion is used.
Producer OutputFile -> Install InputFile uses TaskProvider.flatMap and carries the implicit task dependency; existing install -> checksums -> assets/Lint dependencies remain in place.
All source files including scripts, C++/headers, CMake, config and dictionary data are Gradle inputs with relative sensitivity; Git metadata is excluded. Wrapper directory is separately input.
Clearing the owned host build directory on actual task execution avoids stale generated text when upstream CMake omits Python scripts in generated-output DEPENDS.
Host build directory is LocalState, exported bridge is OutputFile, remote caching is disabled; an unchanged bridge may remain UP-TO-DATE without retaining all host tools.

Stale bridge output is removed before execution; configure/build error fails task before install; generated bridge requires an actual non-comment tab-delimited entry. Install no longer skips the bridge and requires every referenced text file to exist and be nonempty.

Windows native Visual Studio architecture is selected using JVM os.arch; official TARGET_FILE supplies actual .exe and multi-config paths. --config Release works for multi/single configuration generators. macOS architecture/sysroot are explicitly host-native.

Explicit inherited CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE is rejected; wrapper rejects CMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING, system/host mismatch and Android target compiler/flags. If another incompatible compiler slips detection its inability to execute built host tools still fails the task.
Git version discovery is disabled for this host-only wrapper, so .git metadata exclusion cannot silently alter generated resources via local tags.

residual_design_limits.finding: Windows intentionally supports Visual Studio generators only, rejecting explicit Ninja even when a caller might have a native MSVC shell. No repository-documented global Windows Ninja requirement was found. This support boundary should be clear; current Windows runner must actually configure and build.

CMake executable selection and compiler/generator env are inputs, but tool binary bytes/versions and PATH/Python interpreter upgrades in place are not fingerprinted. Remote cache is disabled; retain this local-up-to-date limitation rather than claim complete toolchain reproducibility.

CMake checks rule out common Android/cross toolchains but are not a universal proof that arbitrary custom compiler wrappers target this host. Successful execution of actual host tools/conversion is the decisive acceptance.
Existing four simple generated dictionaries remain the original ExecOperations scripts; this is a focused missing-bridge fix, not a rewrite of OpenCC packaging or config parsing.

execution_gates: Actual Gradle task execution with frozen production hashes and pinned submodule inputs; install output exactly 16 original JSON + 22 text dictionaries, all referenced resources present, original 37 bytes unchanged and bridge identical to official host target.

No-change repeat is UP-TO-DATE; modifying a Python generation script in an isolated controlled case invalidates the full source input, cleans host tree, and actually executes generation; restoring source returns exact bytes.

Intentional generator/configure failure in an isolated case exits nonzero and prevents install/checksums/mergeAssets downstream execution; preserve stale-input/output observations and restore clean production.

Baseline original APK fixture reproduces exactly five missing-bridge config failures with other11 controls; candidate APK fixture loads all16 and matches 38 fixed pinned-source conversion pairs without source/system data fallback.
Fresh Linux/Intel macOS/ARM macOS/Windows CI runs actual host generation and app compile/check tasks from bound candidate tree; cache statuses and existing diagnostics remain explicit.

For any Android runtime claim, compile packaged text via real JNI and load/convert original configs in actual app environment. Host conversion success alone is not Android deployment, physical-device or IME acceptance.
